key_insight: The paper shows how to allocate a limited expert-annotation budget over time to minimize variance in off-policy evaluation when rewards are noisy, missing, or cheaply but imperfectly labeled.
engineering_relevance: This enables more trustworthy evaluation of AI-assisted decision policies in high-stakes sequential settings, such as healthcare, social services, and human-preference systems, without fully annotating every record.
method: Uses doubly robust off-policy evaluation with missing rewards.
Derives variance-optimal annotation probabilities for sequential forward-monotone annotation protocols.
Provides a feasible batch-adaptive implementation for practical budgeted annotation.
evidence_signal: In simulations and two real datasets, the method reduced RMSE by 34-65% on a homelessness casenote task and 17-68% on a housing-application progress task at 40% annotation budget and above, and by 55-62% across all budgets on LMArena.
watch_item: The approach assumes a structured sequential annotation protocol and careful modeling of annotation probabilities, so gains may depend on how well the deployment setting matches those assumptions.
paper_title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
